tldr: WebExplorer introduces a systematic data generation approach using model-based exploration and iterative long-to-short query evolution to create challenging QA pairs, enabling training of an 8B web agent that achieves state-of-the-art performance on information-seeking benchmarks.
contributions: A model-based exploration approach where LLMs autonomously navigate the web to construct information spaces from seed entities, eliminating the need for heuristic graph construction
An iterative query evolution method that increases difficulty by removing salient information and introducing obfuscation (long-to-short evolution rather than short-to-long)
The WebExplorer-QA dataset of approximately 40K challenging QA pairs synthesized through this process
WebExplorer-8B, trained via SFT and RL, achieving best-in-class results among models up to 100B parameters
methods: The method operates in two stages: first, model-based exploration uses LLMs starting from seed entities (collected from Wikipedia with BrowseComp-en exemplars) to conduct iterative search and browse actions, constructing information spaces and synthesizing initial QA pairs. Second, iterative query evolution refines these queries through 5 cycles by removing salient information, introducing strategic obfuscation of dates/locations/proper names, and replacing explicit references with vague descriptions. The resulting ~40K evolved QA pairs are used for SFT with rejection-sampled trajectories, followed by RL using the GRPO algorithm with a composite reward function balancing format correctness (weight 0.2) and answer accuracy evaluated by DeepSeek-V3 as automated judge.
results: WebExplorer-8B (RL) achieves 15.7% on BrowseComp-en and 32.0% on BrowseComp-zh, outperforming WebSailor-72B (12.0%/30.1%). It reaches 62.7% on WebWalkerQA and 75.7% on FRAMES, the best among models up to 100B parameters. On HLE, it scores 17.3%, surpassing WebThinker-32B (15.8%). After RL training, the model searches over an average of 16 turns. The evolution process increases average tool calling turns from 7.9 to 9.9 while dropping Claude-4-Sonnet accuracy from 86.6% to 67.1%.
limitations: A gap remains between the evolved QA pairs and BrowseComp-en difficulty in terms of tool calling turns. BrowseComp-en presents excessive difficulty with accuracy below 20% on most open-source models, so completely mirroring its difficulty level was deemed unnecessary. The approach relies on commercial models for trajectory collection during SFT cold start.
